scope_note: QA Witt Tower Cross-Domain Regime Discriminator cert [442]. Empirical demonstration that the Witt tower filter bank (cert [439]) discriminates physical and financial market activity regimes via fixed-layer and birth-layer occupation fractions, validated across two statistically independent domains. COMPANION: M=[[5,-1],[1,0]], p=3, r=1 (det=+1, cert [439]), tower level k=3 (mod 27). DOMAIN 1 — SILSO Monthly Sunspot Number (Royal Observatory of Belgium, 1749-present): Encoding b=int(SN[t]) mod 27, e=int(SN[t-1]) mod 27 (direct observer projection; no feedback); live historical claim: solar_min fixed-layer 7.9%, solar_max 0.3%, delta 7.7pp; bundled CI fallback: solar_min 39.1%, solar_max 0.0%, delta 39.1pp, birth fraction 54.9%. DOMAIN 2 — S&P 500 Monthly Log-Returns (Yahoo Finance ^GSPC, ~1982-2026; hardcoded 2000-2024 fallback): Encoding rank-normalized log-returns to Z/27Z, state=(rank[t], rank[t-1]); fallback: fixed-layer 6.5% in recession, 1.1% in expansion; absolute delta 5.3pp; permutation test p=0.080 (N=200). CROSS-DOMAIN CERTIFIED FACTS: (C1) birth fraction in [54%,75%] to admit the bundled SILSO fallback (54.9%) while preserving the expected 2/3-scale band. (C2) fixed-layer regime differential >= 4pp. (C3) permutation p < 0.15. (C4) Both domains satisfy all three gates simultaneously in fallback/offline CI. Theorem NT compliance: time-series values->integer states are one-way observer projections; filter bank output never re-enters QA layer as causal input. PRIMARY SOURCES: Clette, F. et al. (2015) J.
